tables.title: Effect of low-power modes on the LPUART
tables.text_helper: Table 456, "Effect of low-power modes on the LPUART", in section 44.5 (LPUART in low-power modes) on page 1916. Columns: Mode, Description. 3 data row(s). Notes: 1. Refer to Section44.3: LPUART implementation to know if the wake-up from Stop mode is supported for a given peripheral instance. If an instance is not functional in a given Stop mode, it must be dis.

rows: No effect. LPUART interrupts cause the device to exit Sleep mode.

The content of the LPUART registers is kept.
The LPUART is able to wake up the microcontroller from Stop mode when 
the LPUART is clocked by an oscillator available in Stop mode.

The LPUART peripheral is powered down and must be reinitialized after 
exiting Standby mode.
notes: 1. Refer to Section44.3: LPUART implementation to know if the wake-up from Stop mode is supported for a given peripheral instance. If an instance is not functional in a given Stop mode, it must be disabled before entering this Stop mode.
